mainTopic: Eruvin 10a: Does a לחי visible from outside but flush inside count, and how wide may a מבוי entrance be?
overview: The גמרא tries to defend רבה בר רב הונא's rule that a לחי seen from outside but flush with the wall inside counts. It suggests that the משנה of the small חצר breached into a large one follows רבי, who requires two פסין. A ממה נפשך argument about the 11-אמה measurement knocks this down, and the גמרא concludes that such a לחי does not count. רב יוסף says he never heard רבה בר רב הונא's teaching. אביי reminds him that he himself derived it, among three lessons, from רב הונא's ruling about a לחי extending along an alley wall. The גמרא then rules that such a לחי does count, despite the refutation, because רבי חייא taught a ברייתא saying so. Next, the גמרא returns to the משנה's rule that an entrance wider than ten אמות must be narrowed. It brings רבי יהודה's view that no narrowing is needed, and rejects רב אחי's attempt to set his limit at thirteen and a third אמות from פסי ביראות. Finally, לוי's teaching that one reed in a twenty-אמה entrance is enough is ruled not to be the הלכה. The correct fix, from שמואל in the name of לוי, begins on the next amud.

steps.title: The case follows רבי, who requires two boards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case follows רבי, who holds that a breached חצר needs two פסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי, who said: we require two boards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה בר רב הונא's rule against the earlier challenge from the משנה of the small חצר (10 אמות) breached into the large one (11 אמות). The challenge asked why the small one is forbidden, when the large one's extra wall on the sides should count as a לחי that is visible from outside and flush inside. The answer: that משנה follows רבי, who requires two פסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this answer, the small חצר is forbidden because of רבי's stricter requirement of two proper פסין. It is not forbidden because a לחי visible only from outside fails to count. So the משנה no longer contradicts רבה בר רב הונא. The next step brings the source for רבי's view, and step 3 begins testing whether this answer really fits the 11-אמה detail.

keyTerms.meaning: we require
boards; upright wall-remnants at the edge of a breach

phrases.english: It is [the view of] Rabbi,
who said: we require two boards.
phrases.notes: One board on each side of the breach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier challenge to רבה בר רב הונא from the משנה of the small חצר breached into the large one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the case to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbidding the small חצר seemed to show that a לחי visible from outside but flush inside does not count, against רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי, who requires two פסין. The small חצר is forbidden for that reason, not because such a לחי fails to count.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing רבי requires two boards
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the תנא קמא permits a breached חצר with one board, while רבי requires two.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: a courtyard becomes permitted with one board. רבי says: with two boards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי really holds that two boards are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת. The תנא קמא says one remaining board is enough to permit carrying in a breached חצר, and רבי says two are required. This confirms the position that the previous step attributed to רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: courtyard
becomes permitted (for carrying)

phrases.english: As it was taught: a courtyard becomes permitted with one board,
Rabbi says: with two boards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי's view stated in step 1.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording a מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי

steps.title: The explanation works only under certain assumptions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the answer. It works only if a hidden לחי does not count, רבי holds like רבי יוסי, and רבי זירא and רבינא are rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this? Granted, if you say that a side post visible from outside but even with the wall from inside is not treated as a לחי, and רבי holds like רבי יוסי, and the explanations of רבי זירא and רבינא are not accepted, then that is why the small one is 10 and the large one 11, because רבי holds like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins attacking the answer with 'האי מאי?' First it lays out the one scenario in which the answer would work. This prepares the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that each פס must be 3 טפחים wide. Two boards of 3 טפחים make 6 טפחים, which is exactly one אמה. That is why the large חצר is precisely 11 אמות. This works only if the earlier explanations of רבי זירא and רבינא are rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? (a phrase that rejects a comparison or answer)
granted; this part works
visible from outside but even with the wall from inside
side post that permits an alleyway
is not accepted

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשלמא' is not the גמרא's conclusion. It is only the side that works, and it sets up the 'אלא' challenge that follows.

phrases.english: What is this [comparison]?
Granted, if you say:
[a post] visible from outside and even from inside
is not treated as a side post,
and Rabbi holds like Rabbi Yosei,
and [the explanations] of Rabbi Zeira and Ravina are not accepted,
that is why the small one is ten
and the large one eleven,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: because Rabbi holds like Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: Two boards of 3 טפחים each make one אמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins rejecting the answer of steps 1-2 by showing what it depends on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The attribution of the case to רבי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It depends on רבי holding like רבי יוסי and on rejecting רבי זירא and רבינא.

steps.title: If רבי זירא and רבינא are accepted, why eleven?
steps.stepSummary: If a hidden לחי counts, the explanations of רבי זירא and רבינא stand, and רבי does not hold like רבי יוסי, then the 11-אמה number is unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say that a post visible from outside and even from inside is treated as a לחי, and the explanations of רבי זירא and רבינא are accepted, and רבי does not hold like רבי יוסי, why do I need the large one to be eleven?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the real challenge. Under the opposite and accepted assumptions, there is no reason for the large חצר to be exactly 11 אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without רבי יוסי's 3-טפחים minimum, a פס can be much smaller. So the extra full אמה is no longer explained. The explanations of רבי זירא and רבינא depend on this view, so attributing the case to רבי fails.

keyTerms.meaning: but if you say (the problematic side)
is treated as; is judged as
is accepted
why do I need it?

phrases.english: But if you say:
[a post] visible from outside and even from inside
is treated as a side post,
and [the explanations] of Rabbi Zeira and Ravina are accepted,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי —
phrases.english: and Rabbi does not hold like Rabbi Yosei,
why do I need the large one to be eleven?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The 'אלא' half of the בשלמא/אלא structure begun in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the case follows רבי (steps 1-2)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי does not need 3-טפחים boards, the specific 11-אמה width has no purpose.

steps.title: Either way, the eleven makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: A ממה נפשך argument shows the 11-אמה number fails whether the point is to permit the large חצר or to forbid the small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if it comes to permit the large one, ten אמות and two טפחים are enough. And if it comes to forbid the small one, it should teach us a case where they differ by a lot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the 11-אמה number fails no matter what its purpose is. This completes the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goal is to permit the large חצר, it only needs 10 אמות plus two small boards of a טפח each, not a whole extra אמה. If the goal is to forbid the small חצר, the case should show a large difference in size, to teach that the small one is forbidden even then. Either way, exactly 11 is the wrong number.

keyTerms.meaning: whichever way you look at it; either way
to permit it
to forbid it
handbreadths
is enough
that they differ by a lot

steps.whatToRemember: The answer 'רבי היא' works only if רבי holds like רבי יוסי (3-טפחים boards make one אמה) and the explanations of רבי זירא and רבינא are rejected. Otherwise, a ממה נפשך argument shows the 11-אמה number is pointless.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא tests an answer by checking whether every detail of the case, here the exact measurement, is explained.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:
if it comes to permit the large one,
ten [cubits] and two handbreadths suffice.
And if it comes to forbid the small one,
let it teach us [a case] where they differ greatly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the challenge of step 4 into a two-sided argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 11-אמה measurement under the view that רבי does not follow רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Permitting the large חצר needs only 10 אמות and 2 טפחים. Forbidding the small one calls for a bigger size gap. Either way, 11 is unexplained.

steps.title: The גמרא concludes that a לחי visible only from outside does not count
steps.stepSummary: Since the 11-אמה number is unnecessary under every approach, the גמרא concludes that a לחי seen from outside but flush with the wall inside is not treated as a לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that a post visible from the outside but even with the wall on the inside is not counted as a לחי? Yes, learn it from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the problem in Step 5. The 11-אמה number only makes sense if a 'hidden' לחי does not count, so the גמרא accepts that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that if this kind of לחי counted, the 11-אמה number would be pointless. The only way to keep the ברייתא meaningful is to say this kind of לחי does not count. This directly contradicts the earlier ruling of רבה בר רב הונא, who said it does count.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (introduces the forced conclusion)
Visible from the outside
Even (flush) with the wall from the inside
Has the legal status of a לחי

steps.confusionAlert: This conclusion goes against רבה בר רב הונא's ruling that such a לחי does count. Keep that tension in mind, because the next steps return to it.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that we learn from it:
a post visible from the outside and even with the wall from the inside
is not considered a side post (לחי).
Indeed, learn it from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the forced conclusion from the ממה נפשך argument in Step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Based on the ברייתא, a לחי visible from outside but flush inside does not count as a לחי. This contradicts רבה בר רב הונא.

steps.title: רב יוסף says he never heard this teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף states that he did not hear the teaching that a לחי visible from outside counts as a לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I have not heard this teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף says he does not know the ruling of רבה בר רב הונא that a לחי seen only from outside counts. This sets up אביי's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף had fallen ill and forgotten much of his learning. His claim here is a personal statement that he does not recall the teaching, not a new legal argument. It opens the door for his student to remind him.

keyTerms.meaning: I have not heard (I don't know this)
A teaching / halachic statement

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I have not heard this teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the ruling of רבה בר רב הונא, which was just contradicted, and רב יוסף says he does not know it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף does not recall the teaching that a לחי visible from outside counts.

steps.title: אביי reminds רב יוסף of רב הונא's ruling about a long לחי
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב יוסף that he himself taught this rule, based on רב הונא's ruling about a לחי that extends along the wall of a מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You told it to us, and you told it to us about this. As רמי בר אבא said in the name of רב הונא: a לחי that extends along the wall of a מבוי, if it is less than four אמות, counts as a לחי, and one may use the alley up to its inner edge. If it is four אמות, it counts as part of the מבוי, and it is forbidden to use the entire alley.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back: 'You yourself taught us this!' He then quotes the source it came from, a ruling of רב הונא. This sets up the next step, where he spells out what רב יוסף derived from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's case is a board placed in line with the alley wall, extending it. From the inside it looks like more wall, but from the outside it is seen as a separate post. If it is shorter than four אמות it works as a לחי. At four אמות it becomes part of the alley itself, so the alley has no לחי at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A side post that extends lengthwise
The side wall of the alleyway
Its inner edge
Has the legal status of the alleyway itself

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אַתְּ אֲמַרְתְּ נִיהֲלַן,
phrases.english: Abaye said to him: You told it to us,
and it was about this that you told it to us,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: as Rami bar Abba said that Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: לֶחִי הַמּוֹשֵׁךְ עִם דׇּפְנוֹ שֶׁל מָבוֹי,
phrases.english: a side post that extends along the wall of an alleyway,

phrases.aramaic: פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת נִידּוֹן מִשּׁוּם לֶחִי,
phrases.english: if less than four cubits, it is considered a side post,
phrases.notes: From inside it looks like more wall, but from outside it is seen as a post.

phrases.english: and one may use the alley up to its inner edge.
If four cubits, it is considered part of the alleyway,
and it is forbidden to use the entire alley.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אַתְּ אֲמַרְתְּ נִיהֲלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's claim by pointing to the source he himself had taught.
steps.raayaObject: That רב יוסף did teach that a לחי visible from outside counts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's ruling (via רמי בר אבא) about a לחי extending along the wall of a מבוי.

steps.title: רב יוסף's three lessons, including that a לחי visible from outside counts
steps.stepSummary: אביי recalls that רב יוסף drew three lessons from רב הונא's ruling. The third was that a לחי visible from outside but flush inside counts as a לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you said to us about it: learn three things from it. Learn that the area between the side posts is forbidden. Learn that the minimum length of a מבוי is four אמות. And learn that a post visible from outside and even with the wall inside counts as a לחי.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his reminder by listing the three lessons רב יוסף himself had drawn. The third lesson is exactly the teaching רב יוסף said he never heard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lesson one: you may use the alley only up to the inner edge of the לחי, so the strip alongside it is forbidden. Lesson two: at four אמות the board becomes 'alley', so four אמות is the minimum length of a מבוי. Lesson three: the board looks like wall from inside yet still works as a לחי, so a לחי seen only from outside counts. This supports רבה בר רב הונא, even though Step 6 concluded the opposite from the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn three things from it
The area between (alongside) the side posts
The length of an alleyway

steps.whatToRemember: Step 6 concluded from the ברייתא that a לחי seen only from outside does not count. Yet רב הונא's ruling, as רב יוסף once explained it, shows that it does count. רב יוסף had simply forgotten his own teaching.
steps.whyThisMatters: In one short ruling, רב הונא teaches three practical rules of עירובין: the area alongside the לחי is forbidden, a מבוי must be at least four אמות long, and a לחי that is seen only from outside still counts.

phrases.english: And you said to us about it:
Learn three things from it.
Learn from it: between the side posts it is forbidden.
And learn from it: the length of an alleyway is four cubits.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: נִרְאֶה מִבַּחוּץ וְשָׁוֶה מִבִּפְנִים
phrases.english: And learn from it: a post visible from the outside and even with the wall from the inside
is considered a side post.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַתְּ אֲמַרְתְּ לַן עֲלַהּ: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ תְּלָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's reminder by spelling out the lessons drawn from רב הונא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That a לחי visible from outside but flush inside counts as a לחי (the teaching רב יוסף forgot).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's own threefold derivation from רב הונא's ruling.

steps.title: The final ruling: a לחי seen from outside counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that a לחי seen from outside but flush with the wall inside counts as a לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: a post that can be seen from the outside but is even with the wall on the inside is treated as a לחי.
steps.whatsHappening: After the back-and-forth in the earlier steps, the גמרא now states the practical ruling. A לחי that only sticks out on the outside still counts as a לחי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the גמרא concluded that such a לחי does not count. Then אביי showed in steps 8-9 that רב יוסף himself had taught that it does count. Now the גמרא rules in favor of counting it, which seems to go against the earlier refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: And the practical law is
Visible from the outside
And flush (even with the wall) on the inside
Is judged as a לחי (counts as a side post)

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: a לחי that sticks out only on the outside, while flush with the wall inside, does count as a לחי.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with the conclusion in step 6, which said such a לחי does NOT count. That was a refutation of one line of reasoning. The final הלכה goes the other way, as the next steps explain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for anyone building a לחי for a מבוי.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is:
one that is visible from outside and flush inside —
is treated as a לחי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי's reminder in step 9, the גמרא states the final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A לחי seen from outside but flush with the wall inside counts as a לחי.

steps.title: How can a refuted view be the הלכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the הלכה can follow a view that was just refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a refutation, and yet this is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own ruling. If this view was refuted earlier, how can the הלכה follow it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in steps 5-6, the ממה נפשך argument knocked down the idea that such a לחי counts. Normally a view that suffered a תיובתא is rejected. So ruling like it looks contradictory.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation

phrases.english: A refutation, and also the הלכה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 10 using the refutation from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 10 that such a לחי counts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A view that was refuted cannot normally become the הלכה.

steps.title: רבי חייא's ברייתא supports the ruling
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה can follow it because רבי חייא taught a ברייתא that says so directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, because רבי חייא taught a ברייתא in agreement with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling stands. רבי חייא taught a ברייתא that clearly says such a לחי counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The refutation only knocked down a deduction drawn from the words of other תנאים. A clear, direct ברייתא from רבי חייא is stronger than that deduction. So the הלכה follows the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
In agreement with him / it

phrases.english: Yes,
because רבי חייא taught a ברייתא in agreement with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, מִשּׁוּם דְּתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: An explicit source outweighs a refuted deduction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the view was refuted, it should be rejected.
steps.terutzMaskana: The refutation only defeated a deduction. רבי חייא's explicit ברייתא keeps the ruling in place.
steps.whatToRemember: A view can be refuted in a deduction and still be the הלכה, if a clear ברייתא supports it.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a wide entrance must be narrowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next rule: an entrance wider than ten אמות must be narrowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one wider than ten must be narrowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. It is setting up a discussion of how wide a מבוי entrance may be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that if the opening of a מבוי is wider than ten אמות, a לחי or קורה is not enough. One must first make the opening narrower. The next steps will bring a תנא who disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: One wider than ten (אמות)
He must narrow it

phrases.english: And one wider than ten must narrow it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the לחי discussion and returns to the משנה for a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מבוי entrance wider than ten אמות must be narrowed.

steps.title: אביי cites רבי יהודה: no narrowing needed
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה disagrees and says the entrance need not be narrowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It was taught: One wider than ten must narrow it. רבי יהודה says: He does not need to narrow it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes a ברייתא showing a disagreement. The first view matches the משנה, but רבי יהודה says no narrowing is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the משנה's rule is not unanimous. According to רבי יהודה, even an opening wider than ten אמות can be fixed with a לחי or קורה without narrowing. This raises a natural question about his limit.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not need to narrow it

phrases.english: אביי said: it was taught:
And one wider than ten must narrow it;
רבי יהודה says:
He does not need to narrow it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with a dissenting view on the משנה quoted in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה holds that an entrance wider than ten אמות does not need to be narrowed.

steps.title: How wide does רבי יהודה allow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks up to what width רבי יהודה allows the entrance without narrowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And up to how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי יהודה's limit. Surely he does not allow an opening of any width at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said narrowing is not needed above ten אמות. But there must be some maximum width. The גמרא wants to know that number.

keyTerms.meaning: And up to how much?

phrases.english: And up to how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the limit of רבי יהודה's view in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum entrance width רבי יהודה allows without narrowing.

steps.title: רב אחי's first suggestion: thirteen and a third אמות
steps.stepSummary: רב אחי first thought the limit is thirteen and a third אמות, learned by a קל וחומר from the boards around a well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחי thought to say before רב יוסף: up to thirteen and a third אמות. And it is a קל וחומר from the boards around wells.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחי proposes an answer: thirteen and a third אמות. He learns it from the rule of פסי ביראות, the corner boards set up around a well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Around a well, a gap of up to thirteen and a third אמות between the boards is allowed, but no more, even though the rules there are very lenient. A מבוי is held to a stricter standard, so it surely should not allow a wider gap than that. Thirteen and a third is therefore the upper limit. The word סבר hints that this was only his first idea, and steps 18-19 go on to reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought (an early view, often later rejected)
Thirteen and a third אמות
An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
Upright boards placed around a well

steps.confusionAlert: סבר means this is only רב אחי's first thought. Do not treat thirteen and a third as the final answer yet.

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר רַב אַחַי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְמֵימַר:
phrases.english: רב אחי thought to say before רב יוסף:
up to thirteen and a third אמות.
And it is a קל וחומר from the boards around wells.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר רַב אַחַי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Up to thirteen and a third אמות, by a קל וחומר from פסי ביראות.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's limit for an unnarrowed מבוי entrance
steps.raayaSupportSource: The allowed gap between פסי ביראות

steps.title: The קל וחומר from the boards around a well
steps.stepSummary: רב אחי argues: the well boards are the lenient case, and even they are capped at thirteen and a third אמות. So an alley, the stricter case, surely cannot go beyond that.
steps.simpleTranslation: The boards around wells may be mostly open, yet even they may not have a gap wider than thirteen and a third אמות. An alley may not be mostly open. Surely, then, an alley may not have a gap wider than thirteen and a third אמות!
steps.whatsHappening: This spells out the קל וחומר that רב אחי used in the last step to set the limit at thirteen and a third אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With פסי ביראות, the rules allow the open part to be bigger than the closed part. That is a big leniency, and still the gap is capped at thirteen and a third אמות. A מבוי gets no such leniency, so it seems obvious that its entrance cannot be more open than the well boards.

keyTerms.meaning: Corner boards set up around a well so people can draw water on שבת
The open part is bigger than the standing wall part
Isn't it logical? This phrase opens the end of a קל וחומר
Thirteen and a third אמות, the widest gap allowed between the well boards

steps.confusionAlert: The well boards are the LENIENT case, because they may be mostly open. The alley is the STRICT case, because its walls must be mostly standing. Keep this straight or the whole argument flips in your head.

phrases.english: Just as the boards around wells
which you permitted for them
the open part being more than the standing part
you did not permit for them
more than thirteen and a third amos,
an alley, for which you did not permit
the open part being more than the standing part,
is it not logical that you should not permit for it
more than thirteen and a third amos?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the קל וחומר that step 16 relied on
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's limit for an alley entrance is thirteen and a third אמות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the gap limit of פסי ביראות

steps.title: The same comparison can prove the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the logic around. The well boards need a cap because they are already so lenient. An alley, whose walls are mostly standing, could therefore allow a wider gap.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that same reasoning points the other way. The well boards may be mostly open, so you will not also let them have a gap wider than thirteen and a third אמות. An alley may not be mostly open, so you will let it have a gap wider than thirteen and a third אמות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אחי's קל וחומר by showing that the same facts can lead to the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the cap on the well boards is read as a balance. Since they are already mostly open, they cannot get a wide gap too. An alley must have mostly standing walls, so it is sturdy enough to allow a gap wider than thirteen and a third אמות. Since the logic cuts both ways, the קל וחומר proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: "That very point gives the opposite": the reason you gave actually supports the other side
You will permit

phrases.english: But that very reasoning gives the opposite:
the boards around wells, which you permitted for them
the open part being more than the standing part
you will not permit for them
more than thirteen and a third amos,
an alley, for which you did not permit
the open part being more than the standing part
you will permit for it
more than thirteen and a third amos!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 17 by reversing it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר from פסי ביראות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The leniency of the well boards can explain why they are capped, so the alley could allow more

steps.title: Or the comparison could make the alley even stricter
steps.stepSummary: Another way to reverse it: the well boards got one leniency, so they get a second one, the thirteen-and-a-third gap. An alley got no leniency, so it gets no extra width at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can argue the other way. The well boards were already given one leniency, so give them another one. An alley gets no leniency at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to break the קל וחומר. This time it points toward an alley being even stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the gap of thirteen and a third אמות is treated as a second leniency. It goes only to the well boards, which were already treated leniently. An alley never got leniencies, so it may not even reach that width. With the logic pointing up, down, or nowhere, רבי יהודה's limit cannot be learned from the well boards.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; or else
To the other side; in the opposite direction
A leniency
Not at all, in any way

steps.whatToRemember: רב אחי's קל וחומר fails. The comparison to פסי ביראות can be argued in either direction, so it does not prove a limit for רבי יהודה's alley entrance.

phrases.english: Alternatively, the other way around:
the boards around wells,
where you were lenient with them by one leniency
be lenient with them by another leniency;
an alley, not at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, opposite reversal of the קל וחומר, which closes this line of proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from פסי ביראות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The well boards could earn extra leniencies that an alley never gets, so nothing carries over

steps.title: לוי's ברייתא: a reed in the middle of a twenty-אמה alley
steps.stepSummary: לוי teaches that if an alley entrance is twenty אמות wide, sticking a reed in its middle is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי taught: if an alley is twenty אמות wide, a person sticks a reed in its middle, and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from לוי about how to fix an entrance that is too wide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said an entrance wider than ten אמות must be narrowed. לוי's ברייתא suggests an easy fix: one reed in the middle of a twenty-אמה opening divides it into two openings of ten אמות each.

keyTerms.meaning: Sticks a reed into the ground
In its middle
And that is enough

phrases.english: Levi taught:
an alley that is twenty amos wide,
one sticks a reed in its middle,
and that is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יהודה discussion and returns to the משנה's rule about narrowing a wide entrance
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One reed in the middle of a twenty-אמה entrance counts as narrowing it

steps.title: לוי himself rules the הלכה does not follow it
steps.stepSummary: The same לוי who taught the ברייתא says the הלכה does not follow that teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught it, and he also said about it that the הלכה does not follow that teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that לוי rejected his own ברייתא for practical הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי passed on the ברייתא faithfully, but he ruled that one reed does not really narrow the entrance. In practice, a twenty-אמה entrance still needs proper narrowing.

keyTerms.term: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He taught it and he himself said about it
The הלכה is not like that teaching

steps.whyThisMatters: A sage can pass on a source accurately while ruling against it. Teaching a text is not the same as deciding the הלכה from it.

phrases.english: He taught it
and he said about it:
that the halacha is not like that teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the ברייתא of step 20
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One reed in the middle of a twenty-אמה entrance does not count as narrowing it

steps.title: Another version: שמואל reports the ruling in לוי's name
steps.stepSummary: Some say the ruling came through שמואל, who said in לוי's name that the הלכה does not follow that teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: שמואל said in the name of לוי, the הלכה does not follow that teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of who said the ruling. The ruling itself stays the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, לוי himself stated the ruling. In this version, שמואל passed it on in לוי's name. Either way, the הלכה does not follow the reed ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree: one reed in a twenty-אמה entrance is not enough. They differ only in whether לוי said it himself or שמואל reported it in his name.

phrases.english: Some say,
Shmuel said in the name of Levi:
the halacha is not like that teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּלֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different chain of transmission for the same ruling as step 21
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה rejects the reed method, whether the ruling came from לוי directly or through שמואל

steps.title: If a reed is not enough, how should one fix the wide alley?
steps.stepSummary: The reed-in-the-middle method was rejected, so the גמרא asks what a person with a twenty-אמה alley entrance should do instead. It then opens the answer by attributing it to שמואל quoting לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, how should one act to fix such an alley? שמואל said in the name of לוי:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question: since a reed does not work, how can this wide alley be made usable? It is setting up the next move by introducing שמואל's answer in the name of לוי, and the actual answer comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 21-22 ruled that the הלכה does not follow the teaching that one reed in the middle fixes a twenty-אמה entrance. The word אֶלָּא ("rather") signals that, now that this method is gone, a valid replacement is needed. Notice that the answer is quoted by the same pair, שמואל in the name of לוי, who reported the rejection in step 22. The fix therefore comes from the same source that rejected the reed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather / instead. It signals a shift away from an idea that was just rejected.
How does one act? A practical question asking for a working procedure.
In the name of. It shows the speaker is quoting someone earlier.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking the answer is missing. The colon after לוי means the actual instructions follow immediately in the next section of the גמרא.
steps.whyThisMatters: Rejecting the reed method would leave people with wide alleys stuck. This question makes sure the סוגיא gives a usable solution that is accepted in הלכה.

phrases.english: Rather, how should one act?
phrases.notes: Since a reed in the middle is not enough, what does one do with a twenty-אמה alley entrance?

phrases.english: Shmuel said in the name of Levi:
phrases.notes: Here comes the answer, but what he actually says continues on the next amud.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תשובה (the attribution line opens the answer)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the conclusion in steps 21-22 that the reed method is rejected. It asks for the correct alternative.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A valid method, accepted in הלכה, to make a twenty-אמה-wide alley entrance fit for carrying, now that a single reed in the middle has been ruled insufficient.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer is introduced here as coming from שמואל in the name of לוי. Its content follows on the next amud.
